Project.name: singularity-cli
Project.annotation: Bun-based `singu` CLI for the Singularity task manager API with local OpenAPI snapshots, generated SDK surfaces, XDG-first runtime storage, and standalone binary builds.
Project.keywords: singularity, singu, cli, task-manager, bun, citty, kubb, openapi, grace

Actors.actor-User: Person managing Singularity projects and tasks from the terminal.
Actors.actor-Developer: Contributor maintaining the CLI runtime, OpenAPI snapshot pipeline, and generated SDK.

UC-001.Action: Stores a valid bearer token through `singu auth login`
UC-001.Goal: To run authenticated CLI commands without re-entering credentials every time
UC-001.Preconditions: User already has a valid Singularity API token.
UC-001.AcceptanceCriteria: Subsequent API commands can load the token from local config, respect env overrides, and attach it to outbound requests.

UC-002.Action: Refreshes the checked-in OpenAPI snapshot from the upstream Swagger UI
UC-002.Goal: To keep local SDK generation aligned with the latest published API surface
UC-002.Preconditions: The upstream Swagger UI remains reachable and still exposes the embedded swaggerDoc object.
UC-002.AcceptanceCriteria: The refresh command writes a valid `openapi/swagger.json` file that Kubb can consume locally.

UC-003.Goal: To inspect remote project state from the terminal and establish short-lived SID references for follow-up commands
UC-003.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured and the local SDK has been generated from the current snapshot.
UC-003.AcceptanceCriteria: The CLI issues an authenticated request to `/v2/project`, prints human-friendly rows with SIDs, and saves last-list context into cache.

UC-004.Action: Resolves a project reference passed as a raw id, SID, or alias
UC-004.Goal: To avoid copying full Singularity ids in common project workflows
UC-004.Preconditions: The user has either a raw Singularity project id, a saved alias, or a recent `project list` cache.
UC-004.AcceptanceCriteria: `singu project get 1`, `singu project get @inbox`, and `singu project get raw-id` all resolve to the same API request target when they point to the same project.

UC-005.Action: Checks current auth health through `singu auth status`
UC-005.Goal: To understand whether the CLI is using an environment token, a saved token, or no token at all
UC-005.Preconditions: The user may or may not have a saved token and may or may not have `SINGULARITY_TOKEN` set.
UC-005.AcceptanceCriteria: The CLI reports token source, config file location, masked token value, and optional validation results without leaking secrets.

UC-006.Action: Creates and manages named project aliases
UC-006.Goal: To keep stable human-friendly references such as `@inbox` across CLI sessions
UC-006.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured so aliases can be scoped to the active account fingerprint.
UC-006.AcceptanceCriteria: `project alias set`, `project alias list`, and `project alias remove` persist aliases in local config storage without depending on the last-list cache.

UC-007.Goal: To inspect actionable remote task state from the terminal and establish short-lived SID references for follow-up commands
UC-007.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured and the local SDK has been generated from the current snapshot.
UC-007.AcceptanceCriteria: The CLI issues an authenticated request to `/v2/task`, defaults to open tasks scheduled today or earlier, supports `--inbox`, supports `--project`, and saves last-list context into cache.

UC-008.Action: Resolves a task reference passed as a raw id, SID, or alias
UC-008.Goal: To avoid copying full Singularity task ids in common task workflows
UC-008.Preconditions: The user has either a raw Singularity task id, a saved alias, or a recent `task list` cache.
UC-008.AcceptanceCriteria: `singu task get 1`, `singu task get @today`, and `singu task get raw-id` all resolve to the same API request target when they point to the same task.

UC-009.Action: Creates and manages named task aliases
UC-009.Goal: To keep stable human-friendly references such as `@today` across CLI sessions
UC-009.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured so aliases can be scoped to the active account fingerprint.
UC-009.AcceptanceCriteria: `task alias set`, `task alias list`, and `task alias remove` persist aliases in local config storage without depending on the last-list cache.

UC-010.Action: Marks a task done or reopens it through `singu task do` and `singu task undo`
UC-010.Goal: To manage completion state from the terminal through the same raw id, SID, and alias references used by task read flows
UC-010.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured and the task can be resolved through raw id, SID cache, or alias storage.
UC-010.AcceptanceCriteria: `task do ` sets checked state to done, `task undo ` reopens the task, and both commands guide the user to refresh list-based short ids.

UC-011.Action: Creates and updates tasks through resource-focused commands
UC-011.Goal: To manage Singularity tasks without leaving the terminal
UC-011.Preconditions: Task-oriented write commands are built on top of the generated SDK and shared CLI runtime.
UC-011.AcceptanceCriteria: Task commands cover the common CRUD flows after read and reference resolution layers are stable.

UC-012.Action: Captures a new task through `singu task add`
UC-012.Goal: To quickly create a task in inbox or directly inside a project from the terminal
UC-012.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured.
UC-012.AcceptanceCriteria: `task add` creates a task from a title, optionally resolves a project reference, and returns the created task id.

UC-013.Action: Moves a task into a project or back to inbox through `singu task move`
UC-013.Goal: To triage captured tasks without copying raw project ids
UC-013.Preconditions: The task can be resolved through raw id, SID, or alias and project references can be resolved through the existing project resolver.
UC-013.AcceptanceCriteria: `task move --project ` assigns the task to a project and `task move --inbox` clears its project assignment.

UC-014.Action: Schedules a task through `singu task schedule`
UC-014.Goal: To set start and optional deadline values from concise terminal-friendly inputs such as `today`, `tomorrow`, or ISO datetimes
UC-014.Preconditions: The task can be resolved through raw id, SID, or alias.
UC-014.AcceptanceCriteria: `task schedule` parses user input safely and updates task scheduling fields without requiring manual JSON payloads.

UC-015.Action: Creates a scheduled focus block through `singu block `
UC-015.Goal: To create a task that starts now and occupies a concrete time block without manually running add plus schedule
UC-015.Preconditions: A valid bearer token is configured and the duration string is valid.
UC-015.AcceptanceCriteria: `block` creates a task with `start`, `deadline`, `useTime`, and `timeLength` derived from the requested duration, optionally inside a resolved project.

UC-016.Action: Edits a task title through `singu task edit --title ...`
UC-016.Goal: To rename a task from the terminal through raw ids, SIDs, or aliases
UC-016.Preconditions: The task can be resolved through the task reference layer.
UC-016.AcceptanceCriteria: `task edit` patches the task title and returns the updated task id and title.

UC-017.Action: Unschedules a task through `singu task unschedule `
UC-017.Goal: To remove scheduling metadata from a task without manually clearing raw API fields
UC-017.Preconditions: The task can be resolved through the task reference layer.
UC-017.AcceptanceCriteria: `task unschedule` clears start and deadline fields and resets time-based scheduling metadata.

UC-018.Action: Removes a task through `singu task rm `
UC-018.Goal: To clean up temporary or finished tasks from the terminal through task references
UC-018.Preconditions: The task can be resolved through raw ids, SIDs, or aliases.
UC-018.AcceptanceCriteria: `task rm` deletes the resolved task and reminds the user to refresh list-based short ids.

NonGoals.item-1: No browser-driven login flow or email/password authentication in the first iteration.
NonGoals.item-2: No terminal UI, daemon, or background sync service in the first iteration.
NonGoals.item-3: No global alias sync, multi-profile account switching, or persistent local database in the first iteration.

Constraints.constraint-1: The project must run on Bun and support compilation into a standalone `singu` binary.
Constraints.constraint-2: SDK generation must consume a local OpenAPI snapshot rather than a live remote URL.
Constraints.constraint-3: Secrets, bearer tokens, and raw high-risk payloads must never be written to logs.
Constraints.constraint-4: The initial architecture should stay resource-first and avoid opinionated task workflows until transport, auth, and reference resolution layers are proven.
Constraints.constraint-5: Saved user config must use `SINGU_HOME` when set, otherwise XDG-first config and cache paths; aliases belong in config storage and SID context belongs in cache storage.
Constraints.constraint-6: The first iteration supports exactly one persisted auth token and no profile system.

Risks.risk-1: The upstream API spec is embedded in `swagger-ui-init.js` instead of a stable `openapi.json`, so the extraction step may break if Swagger UI bootstrapping changes.
Risks.risk-2: The published v2 spec exposes bearer auth but may omit token acquisition endpoints, so `auth login` remains a token capture flow rather than an email/password exchange.
Risks.risk-3: SID references are intentionally ephemeral because they depend on the most recent `project list` or `task list` result, so follow-up commands must explain cache misses clearly.
Risks.risk-4: Named aliases can go stale after remote deletion or account changes, so alias resolution must preserve enough context for users to repair broken mappings.

OpenQuestions.question-1: Should future task commands reuse the same `@alias` syntax and `1`-style SID semantics across all resources, or should each resource expose slightly different reference UX?
OpenQuestions.question-2: Should default human output hide raw Singularity ids entirely, or include them in a low-noise column for easier repair of stale aliases?
OpenQuestions.question-3: Should generated SDK artifacts be committed, or treated as reproducible build output after the infra stabilizes?
